title: Early Edo Japanese Temporal Clock
intro: The early Edo seasonal clock divides the interval between dawn and dusk into six toki and the complementary night into six more. It uses the pre-Kansei fixed offset convention.
structure: Dawn is 36 ordinary minutes before computed sunrise and dusk 36 minutes after computed sunset. Day periods are U (6 bells), Tatsu (5), Mi (4), Uma (9), Hitsuji (8), Saru (7). Night periods are Tori (6), Inu (5), I (4), Ne (9), Ushi (8), Tora (7).
example: If the model's sunrise and sunset are 06:00 and 18:00 apparent solar time, dawn and dusk are 05:24 and 18:36. Each daylight toki is 132 minutes, so the transition from U to Tatsu is 07:36. Each night toki is 108 minutes.
history: The early Edo profile represents the pre-Kansei Japanese dawn/dusk convention. It differs from the later model based on a specified solar depression angle, even though both use the same branch/bell sequence.
model: Use solar declination and a 0.833-degree horizon correction to compute sunrise/sunset in apparent solar coordinates. Extend the day by 2160 seconds on each side, reject boundaries at or beyond midnight, then divide each day/night span into six. Render the localised branch and bell count and schedule the next visible boundary.
limits: No seconds subdivisions are offered. Requires valid latitude and longitude; impossible crossings or invalid extended day boundaries produce N/A. The calculations are a modern reconstruction and not observations of an individual historical instrument.
